title.text: Moving to a new municipality: notifying your old and new city offices

summary.text: When you move to a different city, ward, town or village, you tell your current municipality that you are leaving and your new one that you have arrived. This is the national procedure; your new municipality may add local steps.

body.text:
Resident registration follows you when you move. Moving **between** municipalities takes two notifications: a moving-out notification where you live now and a moving-in notification where you are going.

If you are moving within the same municipality, a different, single notification applies and this guide does not.

This is example content for fixtures, not legal advice.

conditions.description: You are registered as a resident (住民登録) in Japan
You are moving to a different municipality
You are moving within the same municipality (a change-of-address notification, 転居届, applies instead)

title.text: Submit a moving-out notification (転出届)

instructions.text: At your current municipal office, submit a moving-out notification. You can usually do this shortly before you move (example).

condition.description: You have a My Number card

title.text: Keep your moving-out certificate (転出証明書)

instructions.text: The office gives you a moving-out certificate. Keep it safe: your new municipality asks for it.

condition.description: You do not have a My Number card, or are not using it for this move

title.text: Submit a moving-in notification (転入届) within 14 days

instructions.text: At your new municipal office, submit a moving-in notification within 14 days of moving in. The office updates the address on your residence card (example).

condition.description: You do not have a My Number card, or are not using it for this move
You have a My Number card

title.text: Include family members who move with you

instructions.text: One household member can usually submit notifications for family members moving at the same time. Bring their residence cards.

condition.description: Family members live with you in Japan

title.text: Re-enrol in National Health Insurance

instructions.text: National Health Insurance is run by each municipality, so you enrol again at your new municipal office.

condition.description: You are enrolled in National Health Insurance (not employer health insurance)

title.text: Update your address with your bank, mobile carrier and employer

instructions.text: These are separate from your municipal registration. Each provider has its own process.

title.text: Applying for Tokyo metropolitan housing (都営住宅)

summary.text: How application rounds for metropolitan public housing work in Tokyo. Applies to Tokyo residents only.

body.text:
Metropolitan housing is let through periodic application rounds and a lottery (example). Eligibility conditions are set for each round.

The Japanese original of this section was updated on 2026-09-28; this English text has not been updated yet.

title.text: Understanding your National Health Insurance bill

summary.text: What the premium notice and payment slips mean, why the amount changes in June, and what to do if a payment is late.

body.text:
Your municipality sends a premium notice (保険料決定通知書) with payment slips (納付書) for the fiscal year (example).

- The premium is usually recalculated each June from the previous year’s income.
- If you cannot pay, contact the municipal office before the due date.

This is example content for fixtures.

title.text: Moving into Setagaya City: moving-in notification (example)

summary.text: Setagaya City’s local steps for the moving-in notification. Use this together with the national procedure; it applies only when moving into Setagaya City, not to neighbouring wards.

body.text:
Setagaya City accepts moving-in notifications at the ward office and at general branch offices (example). Some services, such as child allowance, need a separate application at the same visit.

This is example content for fixtures.
